applies_to: Task 4 checkpoints at rounds 200 and later

development_screen.purpose: checkpoint screening only; never sufficient for final acceptance

relative_gates.reference: the frozen Task 3 parent evaluated in the identical Task 4 environment

checkpoint_selection.no_eligible_checkpoint_action: retain the Task 3 fallback; do not label any Task 4 checkpoint qualified

distribution_metric_definitions.score_std: population standard deviation across complete evaluation rounds
distribution_metric_definitions.score_cv: score_std / mean_total_score; undefined when mean_total_score is zero
distribution_metric_definitions.score_iqr: score Q3 minus Q1 using linear percentile interpolation
distribution_metric_definitions.score_p10: 10th score percentile using linear percentile interpolation
distribution_metric_definitions.min_score: minimum target-agent score across complete evaluation rounds
distribution_metric_definitions.rank: 1 plus the number of agents with a strictly higher score; tied leaders all have rank 1
distribution_metric_definitions.last_place_rate: fraction of rounds whose rank equals the number of participating agents
distribution_metric_definitions.best_opponent_margin: target-agent score minus the maximum score among opponents
distribution_metric_definitions.best_opponent_margin_p10: 10th percentile of best_opponent_margin using linear interpolation

notes: Every training-seed checkpoint must pass independently before model-family aggregation.
The 10-seed development screen may rank checkpoints but cannot prove that a gate passed.
All absolute, engineering, and retention gates are mandatory, plus at least one relative improvement.
A death with simultaneous self and opponent bomb causes may contribute to both cause-specific rates; total_death_rate counts the round once.
Thresholds were registered after observing the round-100 diagnostic, so that checkpoint is historical evidence and is not prospective validation evidence.
